clue.text: Didn't side with anybody and kept out of it

definitions.meaning: to stay neutral in a dispute, joining neither camp

explanation.definitionFit: Both halves are idiomatic senses of declining to participate, one in a quarrel and one in any activity.

clue.text: Nonsense! Standing outside, the sun is hot

annotationWithheld.why: Nonsense! Standing outside, the sun is hot (4): S (sun) and H (hot) are clear, but no reading of 'Standing outside' yields TO around them without a word doing two jobs; likely OCR or setter garble
annotationWithheld.clue: Nonsense! Standing outside, the sun is hot

clue.text: How the quartet went to surpass the trio?

definitions.text: How the quartet went to surpass the trio?

parts.words: How the quartet went to surpass the trio?
parts.note: a quartet has four members and a trio three, so the bigger group exceeds the smaller by a single member

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for outdoing a rival by a small margin is literally true of four against three.

clue.text: In S Africa I twice left the Italian in a mess

indicators.note: a mess suggests jumbled disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
left in the sense of departed, so these letters leave the word
the letter I is taken two times over

explanation.surface: Someone in South Africa leaves an Italian guest's things in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both I's from ITALIAN leaves TALAN, which 'in a mess' rearranges. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province on the east coast of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: March for exam

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A march held in support of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a demonstration, so the noun march here means a public protest.

clue.text: 550 dried out full of holes

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and L is 50

explanation.surface: Five hundred and fifty things dried out until they were full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles DL with DRIED to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something riddled is pierced all over, as a target riddled with bullets.

clue.text: You catch and you hang on to it

definitions.meaning: to ... a culprit is to catch them
a picture is hung on a metal spike driven into the wall

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as the verb for catching someone and the noun for a wall spike a picture hangs from.

clue.text: What the boxing commentary is to do with

definitions.text: What the boxing commentary is to do with

parts.words: What the boxing commentary is to do with
parts.note: the commentary at a boxing match concerns a single fight, and also the word meaning concerning

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it names a boxing fight; whole, it means concerning, which is what commentary is.

clue.text: Quickly ask if you want the torch switched on?

definitions.text: Quickly ask if you want the torch switched on?

parts.words: Quickly ask if you want the torch switched on?
parts.note: a torch is a battery lamp, so someone wanting it lit might ask for a beam; the idiom also means very fast

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning instantly sounds like a request for a beam of light from a torch.

clue.text: The tips need ironing out

definitions.meaning: useful hints or tricks of the trade
creases in cloth are removed with an iron

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both clever tricks or hints and creases in fabric, a skin or a plan.

clue.text: Charming rooms in the hotel, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a suite is a set of connected rooms in a hotel

explanation.surface: Praise for the delightful rooms of a hotel, as people report.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and charming are synonyms for pleasant and endearing.

clue.text: Monks' reading?

parts.note: monks belong to a religious order, so their reading might be the book of that order; really a list of goods ordered

explanation.definitionFit: A commercial list of unfilled orders is cryptically imagined as the book of a monastic order.

clue.text: Healthy twins? What a surprise!

indicators.note: twins come in a pair, so the word appears two times

parts.note: being well means being in good health

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that both twins are in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a conventional way of voicing surprise.

clue.text: Catch on, thanks to her

parts.note: to net is to catch, as with fish
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone grasps an idea thanks to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'her' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name is clued by a pronoun for a woman, a common crossword convention.

clue.text: Sherlock Holmes was a smart Alec!

definitions.meaning: the fictional sleuth was a brilliant detective, and dick is slang for a detective
a smart Alec is a show-off know-all

explanation.definitionFit: The British phrase for a know-all, read literally, is a brilliant private eye like the famous sleuth.

clue.text: Reveals that one is a landlord

definitions.meaning: a landlord rents property to tenants

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to blurt out a secret and to rent property to tenants.

clue.text: With owner in tow or scampering alone to a tree

indicators.note: scampering is running about playfully, so the letters run into a new order

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A dog with its owner in tow runs off alone towards a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scampering' rearranges ALONE into ONALE; 'or' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog on its lead is attached to the owner, who follows along behind it.

clue.text: Unhappy with the old banger that has the fuel leak

indicators.note: a leak lets things escape and spill out, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable because their ancient car is leaking petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD and FUEL together are rearranged; 'banger' (British slang for a dilapidated car) and the rest are surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Doleful and unhappy are synonyms for sorrowful.

clue.text: The last of the craftsmen?

parts.note: it looks like the final surviving artisan, but it means workers who apply the final touches

explanation.definitionFit: Workers who complete the last stage of a product are, literally, the last craftsmen to handle it.

clue.text: As an alternative, there's a train going out after five

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: going out suggests something shifting away from its place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instead, a train is leaving just after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges A TRAIN to ARIANT, set 'after' V; 'As' and 'there's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is a different form or version, which serves as another option.

clue.text: I camp out going in to a resort in Mexico

indicators.note: going in places the jumbled letters inside the short word
out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist decides to go camping at a Mexican seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'into' has to be read as two words: 'going in' is the container signal and 'to' is the outer piece, with 'out' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampico is a port city on Mexico's Gulf coast with popular beaches.

clue.text: Sit back imbibing, with good reason, health drinks

indicators.note: imbibing is drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside it
back means the word sit is read from right to left

parts.note: sane means sound of mind, possessed of good reason

explanation.surface: Sit back, drinking herbal health drinks, for good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit back' reads like an invitation to relax, but 'back' is a reversal signal, and 'imbibing' (a drinking word that suits the health drinks) is the container signal. 'with good reason' means of sound mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisanes are herbal infusions drunk for their supposed health benefits.

clue.text: Will be near through, to add, before dawn

indicators.note: through means one piece passing into the middle of the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add figures
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: Something will be close at hand, and more besides, before daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: This night, the hours of darkness ahead before the morning, is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Breed to get a taller variety?

definitions.meaning: to make something higher, lift it up

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to rear livestock and to lift something higher.

clue.text: Drive like the devil half a mile back

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: back means the kept letters are read in reverse
half means only part of the word mile is kept, losing its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone drives furiously half a mile back.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of MILE is LE; 'back' turns it into EL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or force forward.

clue.text: Don't worry so much about, being stupid

definitions.meaning: to mind is to be bothered by something, so minding less is worrying less

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is advice to fret less; whole, it means thoughtless or senseless.

clue.text: Figure out the cure is to have money

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral, a figure, for fifty

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor works out that the remedy is to have money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Take the yachts back, disheartened, to shore

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters are removed
back means the word yachts is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Sail the yachts back to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing YACHTS gives STHCAY; removing its central HC leaves the answer. 'Take the' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up is to prop, and a stay is a prop or support, also as a verb.

clue.text: Incidentally, it's how a student proves himself, at an exam

definitions.text: it's how a student proves himself, at an exam
definitions.meaning: a student succeeds by achieving a pass mark

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means by the way, and literally describes succeeding in an examination.

clue.text: Comb the peak for

definitions.meaning: the fleshy red crown on a cockerel's head
the top of a hill or wave

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bird's head comb and the summit of a hill or wave.

clue.text: Rub out or erase the first letter in "craft"

indicators.note: removing the opening letter of the word

parts.note: craft and skill both mean expertise

explanation.surface: An instruction to delete an initial letter in a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link; 'Rub out' is slang for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rub out is gangster slang for murder, so it means to slay.

clue.text: How the motorist sought luggage space to no avail?

definitions.text: How the motorist sought luggage space to no avail?

parts.words: How the motorist sought luggage space to no avail?
parts.note: a car's luggage space is its boot in Britain, so a car without one fails to find room; the adverb means fruitlessly

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning in vain, read literally, describes a car with no boot, the British word for a car trunk.
